necessary_context.applies_to: Theorem 2 and the proposed hard family
necessary_context.content: Definition 1 specifies function family, side information and oracle. Definition 2 permits states indexed by J and sums of oracle responses; oblivious parameters do not depend on previous responses. Definition 3 uses the least K with expected function gap < epsilon for every instance and every k >= K, expectation over all algorithm randomness.
necessary_context.name: Problem class and CLI

necessary_context.content: Section 3 uses generalized component-gradient equation (10) and exact component coordinate minimization equation (11), allowing selection between oracles. Definition 3 designates state w_1. Equation (10) prints A,B,C in R^{d x d}, although additive C must have compatible vector shape; this is a source notation issue, not permission to broaden the model. No unrestricted Oracle Complexity conclusion is extracted.
necessary_context.name: Oracle and output scope

necessary_context.applies_to: Hard-family lead; construction identity only, not an accepted hardness assertion
necessary_context.content: H_FSM fixes all but possibly one eta_j to -(L-mu)/2; the remaining entry lies in [-(L-mu)/2,(L-mu)/2]. The varying 2x2 block has diagonal (L+mu)/2, off-diagonal eta_j; remaining diagonal entries are mu. q has first two coordinates R mu/sqrt(2). Equation (13) gives the reciprocal minimizer. d > 1 is assumed for the joint-oracle construction; footnote 2 distinguishes the first-order-only d=1 case.
necessary_context.name: Parameterized family

scientific_cautions.impact: Do not copy the displayed coordinate update as executable mathematics without checking the intended scalar objective and sign.
scientific_cautions.locator: PDF p.8, equations (12),(14); PDF p.14, Lemma 1
scientific_cautions.reason: Equation (12) prints a vector q subtracted from a scalar quadratic, rather than an explicit scalar linear term. Equation (14) prints a minus sign on the q_i coordinate contribution; equation (11) must be the defining interface until this inconsistency is resolved.

scientific_cautions.impact: The k/n exponent step is not justified by the cited total-degree fact alone; do not promote the seed's proof map to a checked proof.
scientific_cautions.locator: PDF p.13, equation (20), and top of PDF p.16
scientific_cautions.reason: The proof infers sum_j k_j <= k from total degree <= k, where k_j are degrees of axis restrictions. This implication requires an additional invariant. Diagnostic calculation: for n=2 and s(eta)=eta_1+eta_2, total degree is 1; fixing the other variable to -(L-mu)/2 leaves a degree-1 polynomial on each axis, so the restriction-degree sum is 2. This checks the stated implication only, not the truth or falsity of Theorem 2.

scientific_cautions.impact: No uniform all-parameter, all-accuracy iteration bound or unrestricted query bound is certified.
scientific_cautions.locator: PDF p.5 equation (4); PDF pp.16-17, Theorem 5
scientific_cautions.reason: Definition 2 allows sums of oracle responses, whereas Theorem 5's n term assumes incremental access to at most one component per query. The per-iteration query budget and conversion must be stated explicitly. Theorem 5 uses kappa>3; its displayed proof gap threshold is mu/2 times (R/[2n(n+2)])^2.
